paragraphs: A network that recognizes objects across transformations needs a way to discard those transformations without discarding what makes the objects different. This paper addresses that problem in group-equivariant convolutional networks. It introduces a triple-correlation layer that converts transformation-sensitive representations into invariant ones while preserving the signal structure that distinguishes different inputs.

The central mathematical property is completeness: the representation removes variation attributable to the chosen transformation group while retaining the remaining information. Common alternatives such as maximum pooling are incomplete because they can also erase meaningful signal differences. The authors connect their layer to the theory of triple correlation, described as the unique complete polynomial invariant of lowest degree.

Experiments show resistance to attacks that exploit invariance and improved classification accuracy relative to standard Max G-Pooling. The implementation needs only a table specifying the discretized group's multiplication rules. Demonstrations cover commutative and noncommutative transformation groups in two and three dimensions, showing that the approach applies across several symmetry settings.
neurips-2023-a-general-framework-for-rob.tldr: A triple-correlation layer preserves signal information while removing group transformations, improving tested robustness and classification accuracy.

paragraphs: When rewards are rare, a reinforcement learning agent may struggle to discover which actions lead toward its goal. Yet previously collected experience can already reveal useful actions and possible outcomes, even if nobody labeled that experience with rewards. This paper studies how such unlabeled data can help an agent explore a new task.

The proposed method learns a reward model from the agent's ongoing interactions. It then assigns optimistic reward estimates to the prior data and trains using both that relabeled experience and newly collected experience. Both the policy, which chooses actions, and the critic, which evaluates them, benefit from this combined training data.

The authors report rapid exploration in challenging sparse-reward settings involving AntMaze, dexterous hand manipulation, and visual simulated robotic manipulation, where exploration from scratch is insufficient. The findings suggest that prior data can guide learning without arriving with task-specific reward labels. The contribution is also practical: this recipe can be incorporated into existing online reinforcement learning algorithms.
neurips-2023-accelerating-exploration-wi.tldr: Assigning optimistic learned rewards to unlabeled prior experience accelerates exploration on several difficult sparse-reward tasks.

paragraphs: This paper studies decisions made repeatedly with contextual information when an online adversary chooses the costs. Its setting combines adversarial costs with a specific statistical assumption: contexts arrive independently from the same known distribution. The objective is to keep regret, the accumulated disadvantage relative to a comparison policy, small while keeping optimization manageable.

The authors introduce a relaxation that produces an algorithm with regret bounded by O(T^(2/3)(K log(|Π|))^(1/3)). Here T counts rounds, K counts available actions, and Π is the policy set. Each round requires at most O(K) calls to an offline optimization oracle, making the computational requirement explicit in terms of access to that optimization procedure.

The improvement is in the dependence on the number of actions: the previous bound had a K^(2/3) factor, whereas the new one has K^(1/3). The result also matches an earlier bound established for stochastic costs. This is a theoretical advance under the stated context assumptions, extending that regret rate to the adversarial-cost setting considered here.
neurips-2023-an-improved-relaxation-for-.tldr: An oracle-based contextual bandit algorithm improves regret's dependence on action count when contexts follow a known independent distribution.

paragraphs: Diffusion models often generate samples inside a compressed representation learned by an autoencoder. For 3D generation, learning that representation is difficult because suitable 3D training data is scarce. This paper instead places a 3D autodecoder at the center of a method for generating both static objects and articulated assets.

The autodecoder embeds properties of the training data into a latent space and decodes them into a volumetric representation. That representation supports rendering appearance and geometry consistently across viewpoints. The authors identify an intermediate volumetric space and introduce normalization and reverse-normalization operations so that diffusion can be learned from images or single-camera videos.

The approach can use supplied camera information or learn it during training when none is available. Evaluations include synthetic objects with multiple views, videos of moving people, and a large real-video collection of static objects. The authors report better generation results than leading alternatives across the evaluated benchmarks and metrics, supporting the use of image and video supervision for this 3D generation framework.
neurips-2023-autodecoding-latent-3d-diff.tldr: A 3D autodecoder enables latent diffusion training from images or monocular videos, with optional camera supervision.

paragraphs: Adversarial patches alter a localized part of an image to cause a neural network to misclassify it. Although this confines the modification to one area, existing patches can remain visually conspicuous. CamoPatch addresses that visibility problem by constructing patches whose appearance approximates the region they cover.

The patch is composed of semitransparent colored circles, an approach inspired by computational art. An evolutionary strategy optimizes the properties of these shapes, while simulated annealing searches for a suitable patch location. This separates the task of designing the patch's appearance from choosing where to place it, with both contributing to the resulting adversarial modification.

On ImageNet neural classifiers, the authors report attack performance that is better than or comparable to leading methods while producing a lower l2 distance from the original image. That distance measures image change; the abstract does not establish that the patches are invisible. The findings show that effective localized attacks can also more closely resemble the image content they replace.
neurips-2023-camopatch-an-evolutionary-s.tldr: CamoPatch optimizes translucent colored shapes and patch placement to produce effective attacks with smaller image changes.

paragraphs: Claims that quantum computers outperform classical machines depend partly on how efficiently the classical comparison can be performed. This paper argues for shared, open benchmarks that make those comparisons more trustworthy. It also develops a reinforcement learning approach to improve classical simulation of quantum circuits.

The authors express simulation as a tensor network contraction ordering problem: selecting the order in which pieces of a tensor computation are combined. They formulate this using a K-spin Ising model and introduce a Hamiltonian-based reinforcement learning algorithm. The reported simulation time is an estimate of less than four days, with a stated 5.40-fold speedup over the compared leading method.

Beyond the algorithm, the paper establishes evaluation criteria and releases a dozen massively parallel environments alongside benchmarks. These resources aim to reduce the need for separate teams to reconstruct classical simulation comparisons. The work supports maintaining shared reference performance curves; its timing estimate should be understood as evidence about the classical comparison, rather than a universal resolution of quantum supremacy.
neurips-2023-classical-simulation-of-qua.tldr: Reinforcement learning improves quantum-circuit contraction ordering, alongside open environments and benchmarks for assessing classical simulation performance.

paragraphs: DaTaSeg combines semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentation within one model trained across multiple datasets. These tasks require related information about image regions but organize their outputs differently. The paper uses a common representation consisting of proposed masks and class predictions, then applies task-specific merging and post-processing to obtain the required outputs.

To connect datasets, DaTaSeg shares all network parameters and uses text embeddings from one semantic space as classifiers. It also accepts bounding boxes as weaker supervision, allowing less detailed annotations to contribute to segmentation learning. Training combines ADE semantic segmentation, COCO panoptic segmentation, and Objects365 detection data.

The authors report improvements across the datasets, particularly smaller ones, reaching 54.0 mIoU on ADE semantic and 53.5 PQ on COCO panoptic. Experiments also demonstrate transfer to weakly supervised segmentation settings, gains from adding training datasets, and open-vocabulary segmentation through direct transfer. A newly annotated set of 1,000 Objects365 images provides an additional public instance-segmentation evaluation resource.
neurips-2023-dataseg-taming-a-universal-.tldr: DaTaSeg shares representations and parameters across segmentation tasks and datasets, enabling stronger performance and transfer from bounding-box supervision.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning learns action-selection policies from existing datasets. Diffusion models offer an effective policy representation, but the earlier Diffusion-QL approach requires a sampling chain with hundreds of steps. Passing through that chain during training is expensive, and the intractable likelihood of diffusion models complicates compatibility with likelihood-based reinforcement learning methods.

Efficient Diffusion Policy, or EDP, addresses these obstacles by approximately constructing actions from corrupted actions during training. This avoids running the full sampling chain for that training operation. The contribution concerns how diffusion policies are trained and incorporated into offline learning algorithms, preserving their usefulness while reducing a major computational burden.

On D4RL gym-locomotion tasks, the authors report a training-time reduction from five days to five hours. They also demonstrate compatibility with TD3, CRR, and IQL, and report state-of-the-art D4RL performance with large improvements over earlier methods. These findings indicate that the tested efficiency gains accompany strong policy performance, making diffusion policies more practical within several offline reinforcement learning approaches.
neurips-2023-efficient-diffusion-policie.tldr: EDP avoids full diffusion sampling chains during training, sharply reducing reported training time while improving offline reinforcement learning performance.

paragraphs: Evaluating healthcare foundation models requires shared data, pretrained models, and tasks that other researchers can reproduce. EHRSHOT supplies these pieces for structured electronic health records. Its dataset contains de-identified records from 6,739 Stanford Medicine patients, follows patients over time, and extends beyond populations restricted to intensive care or emergency departments.

The release also includes CLMBR-T-base, a 141-million-parameter model pretrained on structured records from 2.57 million patients. Its input is coded health-record data, distinguishing its role from clinical models designed for free-form text. An end-to-end pipeline gives researchers a common way to evaluate the model and develop further work.

The benchmark defines 15 clinical prediction tasks with limited labeled examples. These tasks enable assessment of whether pretraining helps models adapt to new predictions or use labels more efficiently. The abstract presents evaluation infrastructure rather than a specific performance advantage on those tasks. Access to the dataset and model is governed by a research data use agreement, with reproduction code also provided.
neurips-2023-ehrshot-an-ehr-benchmark-fo.tldr: EHRSHOT combines longitudinal health records, a released clinical foundation model, and 15 tasks for evaluating learning from few labeled examples.

paragraphs: Masked language models are pretrained to fill missing text, while many downstream applications require finding information in a passage. Pre-trained Machine Reader, or PMR, adapts existing masked language models toward reading comprehension without acquiring labeled data. The aim is to make pretraining more closely match the extraction tasks the model will later perform.

The authors construct a large collection of reading-comprehension-style examples from Wikipedia hyperlinks. A Wiki Anchor Extraction task guides additional pretraining using that resource. This supplies a way to retrofit an existing model using supervision derived from the text's hyperlink structure, rather than requiring a separately acquired labeled training collection.

The paper reports substantial improvements on extraction tasks, including extractive question answering and named entity recognition, especially when labeled resources are limited. When classification is expressed as reading comprehension, PMR can also extract high-quality rationales that help explain predictions. The authors propose its potential as a unified model for extraction and classification tasks formulated this way, rather than claiming universal coverage of all language tasks.
neurips-2023-from-cloze-to-comprehension.tldr: PMR uses Wikipedia hyperlinks to adapt masked language models for reading comprehension, improving extraction and enabling explanatory rationales.

paragraphs: Understanding an assembly video involves more than recognizing isolated motions. A system must connect actions with objects, tools, collaborators, and the evolving procedure. HA-ViD is a dataset designed around this broader problem, with representative industrial assembly scenarios and annotations intended to support shared understanding between humans and robots.

The collection captures different collaboration patterns, natural human behavior, and changes as people learn assembly procedures. Its action annotations separate the acting subject, action verb, manipulated object, target object, and tool. The dataset includes 3,222 videos across multiple views and modalities, 1.5 million frames, 96,000 temporal labels, and two million spatial labels.

The authors benchmark action recognition, action segmentation, object detection, and multi-object tracking. They then examine how those capabilities relate to further reasoning about assembly progress, process efficiency, collaboration, skill parameters, and human intention. This makes the contribution both a labeled video resource and an analysis of the additional reasoning needed to turn basic visual predictions into more comprehensive assembly knowledge.
neurips-2023-ha-vid-a-human-assembly-vid.tldr: HA-ViD provides richly annotated industrial assembly videos and benchmarks for connecting visual recognition with procedural understanding.

paragraphs: This paper addresses two questions in regularized graphon mean-field games: whether a Nash equilibrium exists and how an algorithm can learn one. An equilibrium represents mutually compatible decisions in which agents have no incentive to change their own strategy unilaterally. Establishing existence and providing a learning procedure are separate parts of making this framework useful.

The authors prove existence for nonnegative regularization strengths under conditions weaker than those used in earlier analyses. Their result includes the unregularized case when the regularization strength is zero. They then design a discrete-time learning algorithm and establish its convergence rate under weak monotonicity, without the additional conditions previously required for discrete-time analyses.

The learning procedure also includes an analyzed method for estimating action values during online learning. This estimation component supplies information needed by the optimization algorithm, connecting equilibrium learning with quantities that must themselves be learned. Empirical evaluations support the algorithm's efficiency. The theoretical learning guarantee remains tied to weakly monotone games, while the existence result addresses a broader foundational question.
neurips-2023-learning-regularized-monoto.tldr: The paper proves equilibrium existence under weaker conditions and develops efficient discrete-time learning for weakly monotone graphon mean-field games.

paragraphs: Algebraic varieties are geometric shapes specified by polynomial equations. Q-Fano varieties form an important family because they act as basic pieces in a mathematical process for decomposing more complicated shapes. Their classification remains unresolved. This paper investigates how machine learning can help map part of that classification and inspire new mathematics.

The study focuses on eight-dimensional positively curved varieties with toric symmetry and Picard rank two. A neural classifier predicts whether a variety is Q-Fano with 95% accuracy, providing an initial picture of this restricted landscape. Visualizations using the quantum period suggest a bounded region organized by Fano index, raising the possibility of future completeness conjectures.

The authors also turn inspiration from the machine learning analysis into a proved global combinatorial criterion for terminal singularities in positively curved toric varieties of Picard rank two. The classifier's underlying success remains unexplained, and the observed landscape is not a completed classification. The work nevertheless combines predictive exploration with a concrete theoretical result, illustrating how learned patterns can guide mathematical discovery.
neurips-2023-machine-learning-detects-te.tldr: A neural classifier maps a restricted family of Q-Fano varieties and inspires a proved criterion for terminal singularities.

paragraphs: MADLAD-400 is a general-domain collection of monolingual text drawn from CommonCrawl. It contains three trillion tokens across 419 languages and has undergone manual auditing. The paper treats auditing as part of dataset construction, discussing both its role in creating the resource and the limitations that the authors' own inspection revealed.

The authors also train and release a multilingual translation model with 10.7 billion parameters. Its training uses 250 billion tokens of publicly available data covering more than 450 languages. These figures describe the translation model's training collection, which has different stated language coverage from the MADLAD-400 dataset itself.

The translation model is reported to be competitive with substantially larger models, with results examined across different domains. A separate eight-billion-parameter language model is evaluated for translation from a few examples. Together, the audited data and released baseline models provide resources for multilingual research, linking a large text collection with concrete translation evaluations and openly available starting points for further study.
neurips-2023-madlad-400-a-multilingual-a.tldr: MADLAD-400 releases audited text across 419 languages alongside multilingual models, including a translator competitive with much larger systems.

paragraphs: Denoised smoothing adds noise to an image, removes noise with a denoiser, and then classifies the result. Given an accurate denoiser, this approach can provide certified adversarial robustness even for large pretrained classifiers. Its practical difficulty is balancing robustness with prediction accuracy as the amount of smoothing noise changes.

This paper proposes selectively using several noise scales instead of relying on one scale. A single diffusion model can implement the resulting multi-scale smoothing scheme efficiently. The authors also introduce an objective for comparing the collective robustness of the smoothed classifiers, motivating changes to how the diffusion model performs denoising.

The proposed fine-tuning encourages consistent reconstructions when the original image is recoverable and diverse outputs when it is not. Experiments combining this fine-tuning with multi-scale smoothing show strong certified robustness at high noise scales while retaining accuracy close to classifiers without smoothing. The result is an empirical improvement in the robustness–accuracy trade-off, with the denoiser's behavior adapted to support the certification approach.
neurips-2023-multi-scale-diffusion-denoi.tldr: Selective smoothing across noise scales and targeted diffusion fine-tuning improve the tested trade-off between certified robustness and accuracy.

paragraphs: Neural solvers for time-dependent partial differential equations must remain accurate as their predictions are repeatedly extended into the future. This paper analyzes common rollout strategies and identifies neglected, less dominant spatial frequencies as the main obstacle in that analysis. Such information is often associated with high-frequency components of the solution.

PDE-Refiner addresses this weakness through multiple refinement steps inspired by diffusion models. The aim is to represent all frequency components more accurately, including those that otherwise receive insufficient attention. Its denoising training objective also acts as a form of spectral data augmentation, which the authors connect to improved use of available training data.

On challenging fluid-dynamics benchmarks, PDE-Refiner produces stable, accurate rollouts that outperform the evaluated neural, numerical, and hybrid approaches. The authors also report substantially improved data efficiency. Its connection to diffusion further supports efficient uncertainty assessment, allowing an estimate of when the surrogate's predictions become inaccurate. Together, these findings address both extending useful predictions and assessing their reliability over time.
neurips-2023-pde-refiner-achieving-accur.tldr: PDE-Refiner uses diffusion-inspired refinement to preserve neglected frequency information and improve long-term fluid-dynamics predictions.

paragraphs: Recognizing an object's appearance does not necessarily reveal how it will behave. Properties such as mass, friction, elasticity, and deformability may need to be inferred from motion and interaction. Physion++ is a dataset and benchmark designed to test physical predictions that depend specifically on these hidden properties.

Its scenarios require observing objects interacting with other objects or fluids before making accurate predictions. The authors compare several leading models that use different mixtures of learned behavior and built-in knowledge, and also collect human predictions. This setup examines whether models use the observed dynamics to infer properties that cannot simply be read from appearance.

Models trained with standard datasets and training regimes do not spontaneously acquire the required latent-property inference, according to the reported results. Models representing objects and physical states tend to do better, but all evaluated models remain far behind humans. Their predictions also correlate poorly with human responses, suggesting that success on other physical-prediction tasks does not establish human-like reasoning in these more demanding scenarios.
neurips-2023-physion-evaluating-physical.tldr: Physion++ exposes large gaps between models and humans when physical prediction requires inferring hidden object properties from motion.

paragraphs: Meta-learning transfers knowledge across tasks, but that transfer can become unreliable when a new task differs from those encountered during training. This paper addresses both recognizing such unfamiliar tasks and adapting them toward the learned task distribution. It identifies limited uncertainty estimates and insufficiently expressive learned priors as obstacles in existing Bayesian approaches.

Energy-Based Meta-Learning, or EBML, represents the training-task distribution through two neural-network energy functions. Their combined score is used to detect tasks outside that distribution. At test time, energy minimization guides adaptation of an unfamiliar task toward in-distribution tasks, linking detection and adaptation through the same learned representation.

The framework is designed to work with existing meta-learning backbones, making it a shared addition rather than a separate backbone for each setting. Experiments on four regression and classification datasets support its effectiveness. The stated contribution is a coherent way to detect and respond to task shift; the reported evaluations do not turn that capability into an unconditional guarantee of safe generalization.
neurips-2023-secure-out-of-distribution-.tldr: EBML uses learned energy functions to detect unfamiliar tasks and adapt them toward the meta-training distribution.

paragraphs: Imitation learning often assumes an expert gives correct feedback, but real feedback can be noisy. Under noisy feedback, learning only from a fixed offline dataset can require prohibitively many samples. This paper develops an interactive alternative that selectively asks the expert for labels while controlling both prediction regret and the number of queries.

The selective-sampling algorithm supports multiple actions and general function classes. It uses an online regression oracle both to predict actions and to decide whether feedback is needed. Its regret bound is controlled by the oracle's regret, while query complexity additionally depends on the model class's eluder dimension. A matching lower bound establishes tightness of the stated results.

The authors extend the approach to imitation learning with noisy experts. A distinctive feature is that the resulting bounds depend on how often the optimal policy visits small-margin states, where competing actions are difficult to distinguish. They do not instead count visits by the noisy expert or learner, tying the guarantees to the optimal policy's encounters with difficult decisions.
neurips-2023-selective-sampling-and-imit.tldr: Selective expert querying enables imitation learning with noisy feedback, with theoretical bounds tied to online regression and difficult states.

paragraphs: Dataset distillation creates a small synthetic training set intended to retain the useful knowledge of a larger real dataset. This can reduce storage and training costs if models trained on the synthetic examples perform similarly. The paper examines a potential weakness in optimizing all synthetic examples together with equal treatment throughout the process.

The authors argue that this static approach can couple the synthetic examples, especially when more examples are being optimized. That coupling can prevent the distilled data from capturing higher-level features learned later in neural-network training. Sequential Subset Matching, or SeqMatch, instead adapts the optimization so that synthetic data acquires knowledge sequentially.

By generating synthetic instances in sequence, the method aims to resolve this coupling and preserve knowledge from different stages of learning. The authors' analysis indicates that it succeeds in addressing the issue, and experiments report improvements over leading methods on several image datasets, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet. The findings support treating the organization of distillation as consequential to the resulting dataset's quality.
neurips-2023-sequential-subset-matching-.tldr: SeqMatch optimizes synthetic examples sequentially to reduce coupling and improve the knowledge retained by distilled datasets.

paragraphs: Sketches communicate meaning with sparse visual detail, and a single drawing may reasonably suggest several interpretations. SEVA evaluates whether vision models handle this abstraction in ways that resemble human understanding. Its approximately 90,000 human-created sketches cover 128 object concepts, with different drawing time limits producing systematic variation in visual sparsity.

The evaluation considers both recognition of the intended concept and agreement with human response patterns. This distinction matters because identifying the target object does not fully describe how a model interprets ambiguity. The authors find that models which better predict human recognition performance also more closely capture human uncertainty about what a sketch means.

Despite that relationship, a sizable gap remains between model and human responses. The paper also evaluates a sketch-generation method that can produce drawings at different sparsity levels, exploring the connection between human-like abstraction and generation. The dataset and protocol provide a way to study which information remains meaningful as drawings become simpler and how closely machine interpretations track those of people.
neurips-2023-seva-leveraging-sketches-to.tldr: SEVA uses sketches with varying sparsity to reveal gaps between machine recognition and human interpretations of visual abstraction.

paragraphs: Generative commonsense tasks ask a model to turn a collection of keywords into a coherent, plausible sentence. Plausibility can depend on where or when a situation occurs, yet everyday-scenario benchmarks leave this ability unclear. SituatedGen makes geographical and temporal context an explicit part of what a model must reason about.

The task provides keywords that include geographical or temporal entities and asks for a pair of contrasting sentences. The accompanying English dataset contains 8,268 sentence pairs, assembled from existing commonsense benchmarks with minimal manual labor. The contrastive format brings context into the generation requirement rather than evaluating only an isolated sentence about a general situation.

Experiments show that the evaluated leading generative language models struggle to produce commonsensically plausible sentences and remain far behind human performance. The findings identify a weakness in generating text whose content fits a specified place or time. The publicly released dataset supplies a focused evaluation resource for this capability, extending commonsense generation beyond the everyday settings emphasized by earlier datasets.
neurips-2023-situatedgen-incorporating-g.tldr: SituatedGen tests context-dependent commonsense generation and finds that evaluated language models lag far behind humans.

paragraphs: Knowledge distillation can train a compact student model using predictions from a larger teacher on unlabeled examples. Those predictions provide soft pseudo-labels when real labels are scarce. The difficulty is that teacher-generated targets can be noisy, allowing their errors to impair the student's performance even when plenty of unlabeled data is available.

Student-Label Mixing, or SLaM, is proposed as a principled method for this distillation setting. The authors evaluate it on several standard benchmarks and report consistent improvements over earlier approaches. The practical contribution is therefore better student training in the presence of imperfect teacher supervision, with performance evidence spanning multiple benchmark settings.

The paper also develops theoretical guarantees. Its analysis includes an algorithm improving the best-known sample complexity for learning halfspaces with a margin under random classification noise, and the first convergence analysis of forward loss-adjustment methods. These mathematical results complement the distillation experiments by advancing understanding of learning with noisy labels, while applying to the specific theoretical settings stated.
neurips-2023-slam-student-label-mixing-f.tldr: SLaM improves distillation from noisy teacher labels and contributes theoretical results for learning under label noise.

paragraphs: Concept-based explanations describe decisions using higher-level ideas that people can understand. Most existing work focuses on classification, while agents making sequences of decisions pose different explanatory needs. This paper proposes criteria for defining concepts in sequential decision making and investigates whether explanations can also help the agent learn more quickly.

State2Explanation learns a shared embedding that connects state–action pairs with concept-based explanations. During training, this learned relationship informs reward shaping, which adjusts the learning signal guiding the agent. At deployment, the same model provides explanations to users. The framework therefore connects agent training and user-facing explanation through one learned representation.

The approach is inspired by the idea that explaining knowledge can reinforce learning. Experiments in Connect 4 and Lunar Lander report both faster agent learning through reward shaping and significantly improved user task performance during deployment. These findings support the proposed dual use of explanations in the evaluated environments: helping train the agent and helping people work with its decisions.
neurips-2023-state2explanation-concept-b.tldr: State2Explanation connects actions with concepts to improve both reinforcement learning and users' task performance in two evaluated environments.

paragraphs: Disentangled representations aim to separate the underlying factors that explain observed data. Contrastive learning has shown promise for discovering those factors, but earlier theoretical analyses often treated individual losses separately and relied on particular assumptions about data generation. This paper seeks a broader account of when these methods can recover the underlying latent structure.

The authors establish identifiability results for four contrastive losses. Identifiability concerns whether the true latent factors can be determined within the theoretical setup, rather than whether a representation merely performs well on a prediction task. Their results remove commonly imposed independence assumptions, extending the guarantees to a broader family of methods and less restrictive data distributions.

Experiments on several benchmark datasets validate the theoretical findings, and the paper also investigates practical limitations. The contribution is a more unified basis for understanding disentanglement across contrastive objectives. Removing independence assumptions broadens that basis, but the abstract does not claim that latent recovery becomes assumption-free or that every practical application will achieve it.
neurips-2023-towards-a-unified-framework.tldr: The paper proves latent identifiability for four contrastive losses without common independence assumptions and examines their practical behavior.
